messages:
maya: Quick note — pushed a minimal Next.js starter that wires Redwood SDK + LangChain adapters for onboarding/testing. Repo: https://git.redwood.local/next-starter-stack (private)
liam: Nice, will try it. What's the expected quickstart? npm i && NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY=xxx npm run dev?
manika: (typo) manika: ^ yes, that plus /api/eval route stub. I ran it and saw telemetry not firing for eval runs.
liam: I pulled it and repro'd. On browser console I get a 401 from /v1/telemetry when the eval completes.
maya: Huh. I thought the SDK would auto-forward auth from the frontend. In api route we proxy to Redwood with `await fetch(process.env.REDWOOD_API + '/v1/generate', { headers })` — maybe we dropped Authorization header.
anika: Which headers are you forwarding in /pages/api/redwood.js? snippet:
```
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const headers = { 'content-type': 'application/json' }
  const r = await fetch(process.env.REDWOOD_HOST + req.url, { method: req.method, headers, body: req.body })
  res.status(r.status).send(await r.text())
}
```
liam: There's the issue — no Authorization or cookie forwarding. Browser-only flows expected token in Authorization header, but our sample uses cookie in dev mode sometimes.
maya: Quick patch idea: forward incoming authorization or cookie to upstream. e.g.
```
const headers = {
  'content-type': 'application/json',
  ...(req.headers.authorization ? { authorization: req.headers.authorization } : {}),
  ...(req.cookies?.redwood_auth ? { cookie: `redwood_auth=${req.cookies.redwood_auth}` } : {})
}
```
anika: Also noticed parity problem between node SDK and browser SDK: node client retries 429 with exponential backoff but the browser helper returns 429 raw. That explains flaky local dev when we do repeated eval calls.
liam: Good catch. Could add a tiny retry wrapper in the starter around fetch that mirrors node behavior. Example:
```
async function retryFetch(url, opts, retries = 3){
  for(let i=0;i<retries;i++){
    const r = await fetch(url, opts)
    if(r.status !== 429) return r
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, 50 * Math.pow(2,i)))
  }
  return fetch(url, opts)
}
```
maya: I'll add that under src/lib/retry.js and wire the eval client to use it.
sam: Can we also add a tiny eval harness script (scripts/eval-harness.js) that runs N evals and asserts telemetry counts? Would help catch regressions for onboarding.
liam: Yes — make it opt-in. Something like `node ./scripts/eval-harness.js --count 10 --assert-telemetry` that posts to /api/eval and then polls a mock telemetry sink.
manika: For local dev we currently log telemetry to console. Maybe add an env like MOCK_TELEMETRY_URL so harness can POST there.
maya: Plan: 1) quick header forward in api proxy PR; 2) add retry helper; 3) add scripts/eval-harness.js + README section. I'll open PR with tests (Playwright smoke that runs harness) :)
ci-bot: ci/test-run triggered for branch maya/starter-telemetry-patch — build 42 queued
liam: One more note — in dev I saw the KV cache growing after repeated evals. Might be the sample retention config in the starter uses non-expiring keys. I'll add a TTL in the sample cache wrapper.
sam: thanks, that'll reduce memory while folks iterate locally.
maya: Opening PR now, assigning to @liam and @anika for review. Leaving a checklist in the PR description: forward auth, retry, harness, TTL fix, README update.
liam: LGTM to review. If we can get that test in the starter it should reduce onboarding friction a lot.
manika: Thanks — filing a follow-up to add a small DX note in docs about header vs cookie auth for hosted vs private setups.
maya: Awesome. If anyone running into this before the PR lands, quick workaround: set REDWOOD_API_KEY env on the proxy server so it can add Authorization header server-side.
liam: verified workaround works. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: test-run started: 12 suites, 1 failing (flaky retry test)
sam: I'll chase the flaky test in the CI job, might need to increase backoff or mock 429s in harness.
maya: Thanks team — will update the thread with PR link and test status.
